title: ReadTheRound
one_liner: Rule-based tactical decision trainer: procedurally assembled VALORANT round scenarios (numbers, economy, utility, site geometry as abstract zones) drawn from a curated bank of pro-round patterns; deterministic transparent engine resolves the trainee's calls and scores the decision.
data_risk: none - zero external data; scenario bank hand-authored as JSON, survives without GRID entirely
llm_firewall: Engine owns all state, resolution and scoring; LLM only writes the post-round debrief narrative and coach-tone hints from the resolution JSON; LLM down = full trainer still works
risks: Engine credibility: judges are esports people, a resolution model that feels wrong undermines the demo - keep the model simple and explainable
Scope: biggest build of the set; scenario bank must be capped (~40 scenarios) to fit 7 weeks
Theme fit: category says 'scouting' - frame scenarios as derived from scouted pro-round patterns to stay on-theme

title: LineupLab
one_liner: Utility lineup library + spaced-repetition trainer: curated per-map/per-agent lineups as step-by-step interactive drills on original abstract schematic maps, with deterministic quiz scoring and an SRS schedule that decides what you review next.
data_risk: none - lineup dataset hand-curated in hours-days; static agent/map names from valorant-api.com are factual text only
llm_firewall: Quiz correctness, SRS scheduling and map geometry are deterministic; LLM writes 'why this lineup works' cards and wrong-answer feedback; LLM down = trainer and drills fully work
risks: Lineup content exists as YouTube videos - novelty is in the interactive SRS trainer, so the demo must lead with that, not the library
Map schematics must be original abstractions, never traced Riot map art

title: GCRadar
one_liner: Game Changers-first scouting hub: team dossiers, roster/agent-pool analysis and matchup prep pages for the GC scene, built on a hand-curated dataset so it works even if GRID access never lands.
data_risk: medium - GC results are sparse publicly; curated dataset is the fallback and the demo, GRID is an upgrade not a dependency
llm_firewall: All stats, filters and matchup tables computed deterministically from the curated store; LLM writes dossier narratives and 'what to watch for' scouting bullets; LLM down = full dashboard works
risks: Technologically the plainest of the top tier (CRUD + stats) - needs a synergy-matrix or prep-report module to lift the tech score
Sparse GC data could make the dashboard look thin unless curation is deep enough to feel alive

title: CompIQ
one_liner: VALORANT pick/ban and composition analyzer: deterministic draft state machine plus a curated role-coverage/synergy/counter matrix scores compositions live during a mock draft and ranks counter-picks with reasons.
data_risk: none - synergy/counter matrix hand-curated from public community knowledge; no GRID needed
llm_firewall: Draft legality, matrix math and ranking are deterministic; LLM narrates draft rationale and 'what to ban next' prose from the ranked output; LLM down = analyzer fully works
risks: The curated matrix is subjective - cite sources per edge and show confidence, or esports-savvy judges will poke it
VALORANT draft analysis is less crowded than LoL but still a known genre

title: PatchDelta
one_liner: LoL patch-delta impact analyzer: diffs Data Dragon across patch versions, clusters and scores every change deterministically (champion/item/map), then ranks patch impact by category and writes a coach-readable patch brief.
data_risk: minimal - official Riot Data Dragon is free, stable, key-free for static data; the diff pipeline is the product
llm_firewall: Diffing, clustering and impact scoring are pure deterministic code over versioned JSON; LLM only turns the scored change-set into a readable patch brief; LLM down = ranked diff table still delivers
risks: Category 2 genre is crowded, though a diff-first analyzer (vs another draft manager) is a fresher sub-angle
Impact story is 'every LoL player reads patches' - broad but less sponsor-heartstringing than Game Changers

title: BuyMath
one_liner: Economy x utility value simulator: deterministic round-economy engine computes every affordable buy for your loss/win streak, then scores what each buy actually buys you (utility coverage, rifle odds) so the team knows the correct collective buy.
data_risk: none - weapon/utility prices are static factual numbers; all math is local
llm_firewall: Combinatorial buy enumeration and scoring are exact math; LLM explains the recommended buy in team-callout language; LLM down = full calculator works
risks: Value model credibility (what does a smoke 'buy you'?) - keep scoring transparent and adjustable
Impact is narrower than lineup tools

title: Mirror
one_liner: Local-first self-scouting profiler: log your matches (fast paste form), get a deterministic playstyle profile (aggression, utility usage, role tendencies, trend lines) and a coach narrative built from your own numbers - your data never leaves the machine.
data_risk: none - user-entered data only; no Riot stats API exists anyway, which is why manual entry is the honest design
llm_firewall: Profile indices and trends are computed stats; LLM converts them into coach-tone narratives and practice focus suggestions; LLM down = profile and charts fully work
risks: Manual entry friction - demo must use a seeded profile and show the entry form taking <60s
Self-scouting is less crowded than opponent scouting but harder to make flashy in 3 minutes

title: ScoutPilot
one_liner: Opponent prep report generator: pick an opponent team, deterministic stat computation over a curated pro-match dataset produces structured scouting facts, and the local LLM assembles a full written scouting report with talking points.
data_risk: high - the interesting version needs GRID or a deep curated pro-match set; curated-only version is shallow
llm_firewall: Every number in the report comes from deterministic aggregation; LLM only orders and phrases them into report prose with JSON-forced input; LLM down = stat dossier still complete
risks: 'AI writes a report' is the most common hackathon pitch in existence - novelty score capped
If GRID access fails, the dataset curation burden jumps sharply

title: MacroLog
one_liner: Amateur LoL macro coach: pull your games via the official Riot match/timeline API, compute deterministic macro metrics (objective timings, tempo, vision patterns vs your baseline), and get a local-LLM coach debrief - private by design.
data_risk: minimal - official free Riot API with stable schemas; key signup is instant and free
llm_firewall: Metrics and baselines computed deterministically from timeline JSON; LLM writes the debrief and drill suggestions; LLM down = metrics dashboard fully works
risks: op.gg/porofessor adjacency caps novelty - the local-first privacy/coach angle is the differentiator and must be said out loud
Category 2 is the crowded genre per opportunity.md

title: SetupBoard
one_liner: Coach's tactical setup authoring tool: abstract original-geometry site board with keyframed player/utility timelines, a shareable setup library, and LLM-generated practice drills derived from each saved setup.
data_risk: none - all content authored by the user; zero external data
llm_firewall: Board, timeline playback and export are deterministic; LLM turns a setup into a drill plan and coaching notes; LLM down = board and library fully work
risks: Canvas/timeline editor is design-heavy and easy to under-polish solo
Audience is coaches specifically - impact story narrower than player-facing tools

title: MetaPulse
one_liner: Patch-to-pro meta shift tracker: snapshot agent/map pick-ban trends across patches from curated (or GRID if granted) data, deterministic trend/regression stats flag meta shifts, LLM writes the 'what changed and why' meta narrative.
data_risk: high - needs a multi-patch pro pick/ban history; curated snapshots make a demo but limit depth
llm_firewall: Trend math exact; LLM narrates shifts from computed deltas; LLM down = charts and shift flags fully work
risks: Data curation is the whole product here - highest GRID-dependency of the Cat 1 set
Meta trackers exist in content form; interactive shift-flagging is the only new bit

title: DraftRush
one_liner: Booth mini game with fully original IP: fast 60-second roster-drafting duel against an heuristic AI over abstract geometric original characters; deterministic draft scoring, local LLM as hype/trash-talk announcer, on-screen leaderboard.
data_risk: none - all content original and local
llm_firewall: Draft rules, AI opponent and scoring deterministic; LLM only generates announcer lines (non-gameplay); LLM down = game fully playable with canned lines
risks: Original-names/original-art rule means zero Riot flavor - abstract art style needed to keep asset cost solo-feasible
Booth category impact story is inherently weakest; Rider recommended but web is allowed

title: CounterPick
one_liner: Operator counter-pick advisor: curated agent-vs-agent and agent-vs-map matchup matrix; enter the enemy composition, get ranked counter suggestions with per-pair confidence and reasoning chains.
llm_firewall: Matrix lookup and ranking deterministic; LLM explains picks; LLM down = advisor fully works
risks: Matchup-matrix tools are a known genre - novelty is the weakest axis
Overlaps CompIQ; picking both would be double-counting one concept

title: DraftRoom
one_liner: Coach-first LoL draft assistant for amateur teams: deterministic draft state machine with heuristic team-strength evaluation from Data Dragon + curated tier data, LLM provides draft rationale in coach language - local-first, no account linking.
data_risk: minimal - Data Dragon free and stable
llm_firewall: Draft machine and eval deterministic; LLM narrates; LLM down = draft tool fully works
risks: Draft managers are the most crowded sub-genre in this contest's category 2 - explicit novelty handicap per opportunity.md
Only worth it as a safe fallback if Cat 1 spikes fail

title: ScrimSync
one_liner: Post-scrim review tool for amateur teams: fast structured round-event entry during review, deterministic aggregation computes round-win factors and habit patterns per team, LLM writes the post-scrim team review.
llm_firewall: Aggregation and factor analysis deterministic; LLM writes the review prose; LLM down = analytics fully work
risks: Data-entry-heavy product makes a slow demo - presentation score suffers
Needs two-scrim seed data to show any insight at all

title: NerveGrid
one_liner: Booth reflex-and-decision mini game: original geometric grid, deterministic reaction/decision rounds with skill-based scoring and local high-score board; LLM generates round flavor and post-run taunts.
llm_firewall: Game logic 100% deterministic; LLM is pure flavor layer; LLM down = game fully works
risks: Reflex mini games are the default hobby entry - weakest novelty in the set
Kept only as the low-effort Cat 3 floor option
